text: Highmark Commercial Medical Policy-PA, WV, DE Medical Policy: S-299-001 Topic (or Title): Knee Replacement, Partial Section: Surgery Effective Date: May 1, 2026 Issued Date: April 20, 2026 Last Revision Date: April 2026 Annual Review: April 2026 Partial knee replacement, also known as unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, is a surgical procedure in which one joint surface of the knee is resurfaced, reconstructed, or replaced. This procedure is an alternative to total knee replacement for individuals with damage confined to only one compartment of the knee. Policy Position Partial knee replacement (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following are met:  The individual has experienced pain and functional disability with ADLs for at least three (3) months due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and  Knee stability has been confirmed by physical examination ( Note: ACL integrity is preferred but not absolute; ACL-deficient knees may be eligible when functional stability is restored through prior or concurrent ACL reconstruction.); and  Knee flexion is greater than 90 degrees; and  Flexion contracture of 15 degrees or less; and  Radiographic or arthroscopic evidence of ONE or more of the following is present: o Severe unicompartmental degenerative arthritis of the knee joint with bone-on-bone joint space loss on weight-bearing radiographs (e.g., Kellgren-Lawrence IV or equivalent); or o Outerbridge Grade IV chondral loss confirmed by arthroscopy or MRI and the individual is not a candidate for joint-sparing procedures; or o Unicompartmental avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of tibial and/or femoral condyle; and  History of unsuccessful appropriate physician-directed conservative therapy (e.g. weight loss, NSAIDs, physical therapy, activity modification) is ONE of the following: o The individual has completed at least (3) months of conservative therapy; or o Conservative therapy is inappropriate, and documentation noting this is provided. Partial knee replacement not meeting the criteria as indicated in this policy is considered not medically necessary. Procedure Codes 27437 27438 27440 27441 27446 0055T S2900 Patellofemoral unicompartmental replacement following a total knee replacement may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following are met:  The individual has previously undergone a total knee replacement where patellar resurfacing was not performed; and  The goal of patellofemoral replacement is ONE or more of the following: o Management of protracted anterior knee pain attributed to the patellofemoral joint; or o Management of mechanical symptoms attributed to the patellofemoral joint; and  The individual has experienced pain and functional disability for at least three (3) months; and  Ligaments are intact and stable; and  Knee flexion is greater than 90 degrees; and  Flexion contracture of 15 degrees or less; and  History of unsuccessful appropriate physician-directed conservative therapy (e.g. weight loss, NSAIDs, physical therapy, activity modification) is ONE or more of the following: o The individual has completed at least three (3) months of conservative therapy; or o Conservative therapy is inappropriate, and documentation noting this is provided. Patellofemoral replacement following a total knee replacement not meeting the criteria as indicated in this policy is considered not medically necessary. Professional Statements and Societal Positions American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS), Clinical Practice Guideline: Surgical Management of Knee Osteoarthritis, 2022 The 2022 AAOS guideline supports unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) as an effective treatment for individuals with isolated medial or lateral compartment osteoarthritis who have failed non-operative management. The guideline no longer restricts eligibility based on age, BMI, or activity level, emphasizing individualized assessment and shared decision-making.
